controls.title: Govern mobile access to organisational systems
controls.statement: Authorise mobile and privately owned device access by risk, enforce approved configurations through central management, and separate organisational information from personal use.
controls.risk: An unmanaged or privately owned device could expose organisational information or provide an untrusted route into important systems.
controls.scope: Organisation-owned and privately owned mobile devices, mobile operating systems, applications, management services and connections to organisational systems or data.
controls.examine: Compare the mobile-device policy and authorised device inventory with risk or legal decisions, enrolment records, management profiles, compliance rules, application controls and organisational-data separation.
controls.interview: Ask mobility, legal and service owners how devices are approved, enrolled, kept compliant and blocked when ownership, support or risk changes.
controls.test: Use authorised managed and unmanaged devices to attempt access, verify that only compliant devices connect and confirm that organisational information remains within the approved managed boundary.
controls.expected: Every connected mobile device is authorised, identifiable and subject to the required management controls, while unmanaged access and unapproved local storage are blocked.

mappings.basis: Requires a mobile device management policy to be developed, implemented and maintained.
Requires evaluated Mobile Device Management solutions to enforce the mobile-device policy.
Requires legal advice before privately owned devices are allowed to access systems or data.
Prevents privately owned devices from storing OFFICIAL: Sensitive or PROTECTED data.
Requires configuration and connection requirements for organisation-controlled mobile devices and authorisation before connection.
Requires network protections for selected asset types based on risk, including externally owned devices and assets connected through Wi-Fi.
Requires risk-based network protections for asset types including externally owned devices and Wi-Fi-connected assets.

controls.title: Protect information on mobile devices
controls.statement: Encrypt organisational information on mobile devices and across public networks, use protected connections, and support secure removal when access or custody is lost.
controls.risk: A lost, stolen or intercepted mobile device could disclose sensitive information and credentials or allow continued access to organisational services.
controls.scope: Mobile-device internal and removable storage, managed containers, public-network traffic, VPN configuration, screen locks and remote purge or wipe capability.
controls.examine: Inspect management policies and compliance reports for encryption, protected connectivity, screen lock, remote wipe, key handling and responses to lost, stolen or retired devices.
controls.interview: Ask mobility and incident teams how they detect loss, revoke access, protect encryption keys and decide when to lock or wipe a device.
controls.test: Sample managed devices to verify storage encryption and protected public-network traffic, then perform an authorised lost-device exercise that revokes access and invokes the documented containment action.
controls.expected: Organisational information remains encrypted on devices and public networks, and lost or retired devices can no longer provide usable data or access.

mappings.basis: Requires mobile-device internal storage and removable media to use ASD-approved encryption.
Requires sensitive or classified mobile-device traffic over public infrastructure to use ASD-approved encryption.
Requires mobile devices to use always-on VPN functionality.
Requires full-device or container encryption to protect information on mobile devices.
Requires mobile-device information to be purged or wiped after a defined number of unsuccessful logon attempts.

controls.title: Authorise and secure wireless access
controls.statement: Approve each type of wireless access, harden access points, authenticate users or devices, encrypt traffic and separate public wireless services from organisational networks.
controls.risk: Weak or unauthorised wireless access could let someone bypass physical and network boundaries, intercept information or enter internal systems from nearby.
controls.scope: Corporate and public Wi-Fi, wireless access points, authentication services, encryption, management interfaces, network separation and other authorised wireless technologies.
controls.examine: Reconcile authorised wireless services and access points with network discovery, hardening standards, administrative interfaces, authentication, encryption and public-network segmentation.
controls.interview: Ask network owners how new wireless services are approved, rogue access points are detected and obsolete protocols or shared credentials are removed.
controls.test: From authorised test devices, verify authentication and encryption on corporate wireless, separation of public wireless, rejection of unsupported protocols and detection of a controlled unauthorised access point.
controls.expected: Only authorised hardened wireless services operate, corporate access strongly authenticates and encrypts connections, and public or untrusted wireless cannot reach internal networks.

mappings.basis: Requires wireless access-point settings to be hardened.
Requires WPA3-Enterprise 192-bit mode to protect wireless-network traffic.
Requires public wireless networks to be segregated from all other organisational networks.
Requires configuration and connection requirements and prior authorisation for each type of wireless access.
Requires user or device authentication and encryption for wireless access.
Requires secure network-management and communication protocols such as 802.1X and WPA2 Enterprise or later.
